issue.title: bob highlights clip: design recapture and versioning for already-captured URLs

task_type_fields.proposal:
Design recapture and versioning for already-captured URLs in `bob highlights clip` (proposed by phase bob-cli-35.5 of epic bob-cli-35, recorded by bob-cli-35.land).

Today dedupe is strict by design: a URL whose dedupe key matches any `ref/**.md` frontmatter `source_url` is refused even with `--force` (hint: "open the note, or delete it to recapture"), and an xlib hit is refused unless `--force` targets the same intake path. There is no way to take a fresh snapshot of an updated article while keeping the existing ref note, its Highlights annotations, and its `^ref` lifecycle task. A design should decide how a recapture is stored (new versioned PDF stem vs replacing the library PDF), how the ref note and existing highlights/sidecar carry over, how `captured` changes, and how `scan` treats the transition.

Relevant code: src/native/highlights_ref/clip.rs (collect_recorded_source_urls, check_dedupe), src/native/highlights_ref/clip_url.rs (dedupe key), scan/sync in src/native/highlights_ref/; contract in docs/highlights-clip.md ("Marker fields and dedupe").
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: plan:202610/web_url_highlights_clip.md decided "Library PDFs are never overwritten" and refuses ref-note duplicates even with --force; recapture and versioning were deliberately deferred. Epic bob-cli-35 implemented that strict v1 contract; changing it is a separate design decision touching scan and the vault's ref-note lifecycle.

issue.creation_reason: Epic bob-cli-35's live-verify phase proposed recapture and versioning as a follow-up; v1 deliberately refuses already-captured URLs, so updating a captured article needs its own design.

payload.entry: legacy-capture (bob-cli-4w.9) landed: a URL recorded only by legacy notes without source_pdf now captures with a warning instead of refusing. PDF-backed recapture and versioning remain open.
fold_ref_clip_into_create landed: the entry point is now `bob ref create <URL>` (web-article route) for recapture and versioning. `clip` survives only as a permanent hidden alias.
